mechanics.name: Move pipeline
mechanics.rule: A move runs fixed stages in order and any stage can abort the rest: can the user move at all, resolve targets and redirects, Protect-style block, type immunity, powder and Prankster immunity, accuracy, then per hit: damage, move effects, self-drops, secondaries, forced switch; after all hits: faint resolution, then recoil. An aborted target gets no later stage, so an immune, protected or missed target takes no damage, effects or self-drops.

mechanics.name: Target resolution
mechanics.rule: Before a move runs, its target type (normal, self, adjacentAlly, allAdjacentFoes, allAdjacent, and so on) plus the board state give the list of Pokémon it hits. Fainted and absent Pokémon are not targets. Spread moves hit more than one target and get x0.75 damage only when two or more are actually hit. Single-target moves from a foe can be redirected by Follow Me, Rage Powder, Lightning Rod and similar; spread moves cannot. If the chosen target is gone, the move retargets to a living foe or fails.

mechanics.name: Accuracy and evasion
mechanics.rule: A move with numeric accuracy hits if a roll from 0 to 99 is below the final accuracy; accuracy true skips the roll. Final accuracy is move accuracy times the accuracy and evasion stage multipliers (3/3 at 0, 4/3 at +1 up to 9/3 at +6; inverse for evasion), times ability and item modifiers. Each target of a spread move gets its own roll. A miss stops the rest of the move for that target. Some abilities, items and weather change or skip the roll.

mechanics.name: Self stat drop
mechanics.rule: Some moves lower the user's own stats as a guaranteed effect once they hit (Close Combat, Superpower, Overheat, Draco Meteor, Leaf Storm, Hammer Arm, Make It Rain, Clanging Scales, Armor Cannon, Headlong Rush, Ice Hammer). The drop runs after damage, only for a target that was actually hit. An immune, missed, Protect-blocked or never-started move gives no drop. A spread move drops the user once, not once per target. Drops stop at -6. The drop is self-caused, so foe-drop blockers and reactors (Clear Body, Mirror Armor, Defiant, Competitive) ignore it, and Contrary inverts it.

mechanics.name: Secondary effects
mechanics.rule: Some moves add a chance of an extra effect on the target (status, flinch, a stat drop) or on the user (a stat raise). The effect is rolled after damage and after any self-drop, once per target. It applies only to a target that was actually hit and is still alive, and not when the hit landed on a Substitute. A chance of 100 skips the roll. Existing status, type immunity to the status, and the stat floor can still make it do nothing. Shield Dust blocks it on the holder; Sheer Force removes it from the user's moves and boosts their power ×1.3; held items and abilities can add a flinch chance to moves with no secondary.

mechanics.name: Recoil, drain and healing
mechanics.rule: HP changes from a move's own result. Recoil: after the hit loop the user loses a fraction of the damage actually dealt (Double-Edge 33%, Head Smash 1/2, Wild Charge 1/4), minimum 1, and only if damage was dealt. Drain: the user heals a fraction of the damage dealt (50% or 75%). Both use damage actually removed, so the target's remaining HP caps it. Pure healing moves restore a fraction of max HP and fail at full HP; some depend on weather. None of it happens for an immune, missed or blocked move. Rock Head and Magic Guard stop recoil, Liquid Ooze turns drain into a loss, Big Root boosts drain, Heal Block stops healing, and Shell Bell and Life Orb add after-hit HP changes.

mechanics.name: Multi-hit moves
mechanics.rule: A multi-hit move runs the per-hit stages once per hit. Hit count is fixed (2, 3 or 10) or random for the 2-5 range (2 and 3 at 35% each, 4 and 5 at 15% each). Each hit has its own damage roll, crit roll and secondary roll. Accuracy is rolled once for the sequence, except Triple Axel and Population Bomb, which roll before each hit and stop at the first miss. Hits stop when the target faints. An immune or Protected target gets no hits. The user's own stat changes (Scale Shot) and Life Orb apply once, after the last hit; contact items and abilities and Focus Sash react per hit. Skill Link makes the 2-5 range always 5; Parental Bond adds a weaker second hit to single-hit moves.

mechanics.name: Critical hits
mechanics.rule: Each hit rolls for a crit unless the move is a status move or always crits. The chance depends on a crit stage: 0 gives 1/24, +1 gives 1/8, +2 gives 1/2, +3 or more always crits. The stage rises from high-crit moves (+1), Focus Energy (+2), Dragon Cheer (+1 or +2), Super Luck (+1), Scope Lens (+1) and Leek (+2 for Farfetch'd). Battle Armor and Shell Armor block crits, even always-crit moves, unless Mold Breaker. Merciless always crits a poisoned target. A crit multiplies damage by 1.5 (Sniper: 2.25 in total), ignores the attacker's Attack drops and the target's Defense boosts, and ignores screens, but keeps burn. Anger Point sets Attack to +6 when the holder takes a crit.

mechanics.name: Major status conditions
mechanics.rule: A Pokémon can have at most one major status: burn, poison, badly poisoned (Toxic), paralysis, sleep or freeze. A second one never overwrites the first. It stays through switching and KO replacement, and ends only through a cure (Heal Bell, Rest) or a timer (sleep, freeze thaw). Type immunities block it: Fire cannot be burned, Electric cannot be paralyzed, Poison and Steel cannot be poisoned (Corrosion bypasses), Ice cannot be frozen. Effects: burn halves physical damage and deals 1/16 at end of turn; poison deals 1/8; Toxic deals 1/16 more each turn; paralysis halves Speed and can stop the move; sleep and freeze stop the move until they end. Guts and Magic Guard change these effects; other status-related abilities, berries, Safeguard, terrains and Toxic Spikes have their own entries.

mechanics.name: Volatile status conditions
mechanics.rule: Temporary conditions a Pokémon can have several of at once. They do not use the major-status slot and are cleared on switch-out or faint. Confusion lasts 2-5 turns and each move attempt has a 1/3 chance to hit the user instead (40-power typeless physical hit using its own Attack and Defense, no crit, no STAB, the move is lost). Taunt (3 turns) blocks status moves. Encore (3 turns) forces the last move. Disable (4 turns) blocks the last move; Torment blocks repeating a move. Leech Seed drains 1/8 max HP each end of turn to the slot that seeded it (Grass is immune). Trapping moves (Fire Spin and similar, 4-5 turns, 1/8 per turn) and Mean Look stop the target switching, except Ghost types. Re-applying an existing one changes nothing.

mechanics.name: Weather
mechanics.rule: Sun, rain, sand and snow, one at a time; a new weather replaces the old, the same one fails. Set by a move or an entry ability for 5 turns counting the turn it was set (8 with the matching rock: Heat Rock, Damp Rock, Smooth Rock, Icy Rock). The weather ends at the start of the last turn's residual phase, before its effect. Sun: Fire x1.5, Water x0.5, nothing can freeze. Rain: Water x1.5, Fire x0.5. Sand: 1/16 max HP each turn to anything not Rock, Ground or Steel (Overcoat, Magic Guard, Sand Veil, Sand Rush, Sand Force also immune); Rock-types get x1.5 Sp. Def. Snow: Ice-types get x1.5 Defense, no damage. Speed doubles with Swift Swim (rain), Chlorophyll (sun), Sand Rush (sand), Slush Rush (snow). Rain Dish (rain) and Ice Body (snow) heal 1/16. Sand Force x1.3 on Rock, Ground, Steel moves in sand. Sand Veil and Snow Cloak cut incoming accuracy to x0.8 in their weather. Thunder and Hurricane never miss in rain and have 50% accuracy in sun; Blizzard never misses in snow. Weather Ball becomes a 100-power move of the weather's type. Moonlight, Synthesis and Morning Sun heal 1/2, 2/3 in sun, 1/4 in other weather.

mechanics.name: Items that act when a move hits
mechanics.rule: Life Orb: the holder loses 1/10 max HP after a move that dealt damage (not with Magic Guard). Shell Bell heals 1/8 of the damage dealt. Rocky Helmet: a contact hit costs the attacker 1/6 max HP. Focus Sash: a full-HP holder survives a KO on 1 HP, once; Focus Band: a 10% chance, not used up. King's Rock: a 10% flinch on damaging moves with no flinch chance of their own, if the target has not moved. Air Balloon: Ground moves miss the holder, and the first damaging hit pops it. Iron Ball grounds the holder, so a Flying type takes Ground moves and Levitate stops working. Leftovers heals 1/16 max HP at end of turn. Binding Band: trapping damage is 1/6 max HP, not 1/8. mechanics.name: Redirection
mechanics.rule: In doubles a single-target move can be pulled to another mon before it does anything else. Follow Me and Rage Powder (+2 priority, used on a turn) make every single-target move from a foe come to the user that turn; if several foes did, the last user wins, and Rage Powder does not work on Grass types or Overcoat holders. Lightning Rod pulls in Electric moves and Storm Drain Water moves, from any mon but the holder, ally or foe, the fastest holder first, and Follow Me beats them. A move aimed at an ally can be drawn away too. Spread moves and self-targeted moves are never redirected, and in singles nothing is. mechanics.name: Mega Evolution
mechanics.rule: A mon holding the Mega Stone for its species may Mega Evolve once per side per battle, by choosing its move with the Mega flag. The evolution happens before any move that turn, in Speed order, and the mon then uses its move as its new form. The form lasts through switching and the ability is locked in. A species with two Mega forms uses the one its stone names. A team whose stone leads to an ability the engine does not model is rejected at the start.
